You are one worker in a Ringer publish job. Your ONLY writable areas: your current task directory and the staging root <HOME>/Projects/fable-ringer (create it; if it exists, empty it first). Source trees are READ-ONLY.

GOAL: stage a public GitHub repo of the user's ALTERED Ringer setup.

STEPS:
1. Copy the working tree of <HOME>/fleet/swarm into the staging root, EXCLUDING: .git, any *runs*/ state, __pycache__, .DS_Store. Keep LICENSE.md at the root VERBATIM (PolyForm Shield — legally required). Move the upstream README.md to docs/UPSTREAM-README.md.
2. Create overlay/ with the user's customization layer:
   - overlay/bin/claude-kimi and overlay/bin/claude-qwen: copy from <HOME>/.local/bin/, then GENERICIZE — replace any <HOME> path with $HOME-based equivalents, and the final exec line with `exec claude "$@"` plus a comment saying to use an absolute path if claude is not on PATH. Keep every explanatory comment (auth isolation, K2.7 ban, small-model pin) — they are the documentation.
   - overlay/config/config.toml.example: copy <HOME>/.config/ringer/config.toml, replace every <HOME>/... bin path with a <PATH-TO>/... placeholder. Keep all comments.
   - overlay/rules/model-routing.md: copy <HOME>/.claude/rules/model-routing.md unchanged.
   - overlay/skills/ringer/SKILL.md: copy <HOME>/.claude/skills/ringer/SKILL.md unchanged.
   - overlay/probes/: copy <HOME>/.ringer/probes/ (the qwenclaude/, publish/ and kimiclaude *.json probe files), replacing <HOME> with <HOME> in the JSON manifests.
3. Do NOT create README.md at the root (another worker owns it). Do NOT run git.
4. SANITIZE everywhere you copied: no live API keys (sk-kimi-*, sk-sp-*, sk-ant-*), no <HOME> in overlay/ files. If a source file contains a credential, replace it with a placeholder and note it in a file called ASSEMBLY-NOTES.txt in your task directory.

The executed check is the only verdict.
tasks.verified: staging tree complete, LICENSE verbatim at root, upstream README relocated, overlay genericized, no credentials, no .git, no root README.

tasks.spec:
You are one worker in a Ringer publish job. Write EXACTLY ONE file: <HOME>/Projects/fable-ringer/README.md (the directory will exist; if not, create only the directory and your file). Everything else is read-only research material.

GOAL: a thorough, public-facing README.md for 'fable-ringer' — Austin's Fable-bossed configuration of the Ringer verified-swarm orchestrator. The FOCUS is how Austin set up and operates this system; the upstream tool is credited at the end.

RESEARCH (read-only): <HOME>/.claude/rules/model-routing.md (the canonical routing doctrine), <HOME>/fleet/swarm/docs/MODEL-NOTES.md (evidence trail, esp. the 2026-07-22 entries), <HOME>/.claude/skills/ringer/SKILL.md, the wrappers in <HOME>/.local/bin/claude-kimi and claude-qwen, <HOME>/.config/ringer/config.toml.

MUST COVER (in your own structure, but all of it):
- The architecture: Claude Fable 5 as the sole boss/orchestrator that never types implementation; cross-family workers (GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra via codex, Kimi K3 and Qwen via the Claude Code harness, Sonnet/Opus native) doing all execution; executed exit-0 checks as the ONLY pass verdict ('worker claims are not evidence').
- Cell-based routing: cell = model × effort; the routing table's task-shape lanes; the ADAPTIVE-effort rule (sonnet/opus/k3 efforts chosen per task by the boss, never predetermined; qwen = one full-thinking cell).
- The Claude-Code-as-universal-harness pattern: tiny wrapper scripts (overlay/bin/) pointing ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at Anthropic-compatible endpoints (Kimi's api.kimi.com/coding, Alibaba's token-plan endpoint), why this beat the native CLIs (qwencode stalls; 4.8x faster kimi research), and the hard-won operational lessons: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR isolation because an OAuth keychain login can silently shadow env auth tokens (the 401 incident); pinning ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL because endpoints silently alias unknown model slugs; never trusting an endpoint's echoed model name.
- The scoreboard/evidence loop: runs.jsonl, promotion ladder (untested -> probation -> proven), explore-or-fossilize rule, capacity screens with identical tasks/checks for cross-lane comparability.
- Install/setup: what to clone, where the overlay files go (config, wrappers on PATH, rules, skills), which subscriptions/API keys the operator needs (named by KIND only — never reproduce a key), and the doctrine that every new lane needs a passing Ringer probe with an executed check before real work.
- Repo layout section describing the tree (altered upstream at root, overlay/ for the personal layer, docs/UPSTREAM-README.md).
- CLOSING SECTION: credit — Ringer and Ringside are created by Nate Jones (Nate Jones Media LLC), upstream at https://github.com/NateBJones-Projects/ringer, licensed PolyForm Shield 1.0.0; this repo redistributes the altered code under that same license with the Required Notice preserved in LICENSE.md.

HARD RULES: NEVER include a real credential or anything matching sk-kimi-/sk-sp-/sk-ant- followed by a long token (prefix-style references like 'sk-ant-oat01-…' as a truncated illustration are fine). No private infrastructure details (no internal IPs, usernames, or VM hostnames). Write for a competent stranger who has never seen this machine. The executed check is the only verdict.
tasks.verified: README >= 4000 chars, covers architecture/adaptive routing/harness pattern/auth lessons/install/layout, links upstream, credits Nate in the closing quarter, states PolyForm Shield, no credentials.
